title: Affine graph conormal algebras glue without separatedness
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be a morphism of schemes and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion]. For affine opens $V\subset T$ and $U\subset f^{-1}(V)$ put $Z_U=Z\times_XU$ and $Y_U=U\times_VZ_U$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The graph $s_U:Z_U\to Y_U$ is closed; write $J_U$ for its ideal sheaf. The conormal algebras $\bigoplus_{n\ge0}J_U^n/J_U^{n+1}$ [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra] have canonical identifications on affine refinements of overlaps, carrying each homogeneous class to its restriction. These identifications satisfy identity and cocycle laws and glue, including their units and multiplications, to a quasi-coherent graded $\mathcal O_Z$-algebra $\mathcal G(f,i)$ independent of the affine choices. Its degree-zero part is $\mathcal O_Z$. The relative Proj $P(f,i)=\operatorname{Proj}_Z\mathcal G(f,i)$ [def-nagata-relative-proj] exists with the stated affine restrictions. Both $\mathcal G(f,i)$ and $P(f,i)$ are canonically functorial under isomorphisms of the diagram $Z\hookrightarrow X\to T$. If $f$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and $i$ is its first-Fitting singular inclusion [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme], then $P(f,i)$ is canonically the actual branch scheme $B_f$ of [def-sfb-nodal-branch-scheme], compatibly with its projection to $Z$. No separatedness, nodal, flatness or quasi-compactness assumption is required. The global graph need not be closed.

proof.text: Write $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Since $i$ is closed, $Z_U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B=A/K$ for an ideal $K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $Y_U=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R B)$. The graph corresponds to $\mu:A\otimes_R B\to B$, $a\otimes b\mapsto\bar a b$: its two components are $i|_{Z_U}$ and the identity, as required by [def-pc-fibre-product]. The map is surjective since $\mu(1\otimes b)=b$. The affine criterion in [def-weil-closed-immersion] therefore makes $s_U$ closed. This proves closedness locally without asserting closedness of the global graph.

source.place: Tags 01I4, 01JQ, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes and lemma-fibre-product-affines; Tag 01QO, affine criterion for closed immersions

proof.text: Put $Y=X\times_T Z$ and $s=(i,1_Z):Z\to Y$. Its composite with $Y\to X$ is $i$, a closed immersion and hence an immersion. Apply [lem-zl-immersion-cancellation] to obtain that $s$ is an immersion. By the factorization defining immersion in [def-weil-closed-immersion], choose an open $W\subseteq Y$ through which $s$ factors as a closed immersion $j:Z\hookrightarrow W$. Let $J$ be its ideal. Apply [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra] to $j$, obtaining the quasi-coherent graded $\mathcal O_Z$-algebra $G$ with product $[a][b]=[ab]$ and $G_0=\mathcal O_Z$. This constructs a global algebra from an actual closed immersion, with no separatedness or finiteness assumption.

source.place: Section 0630, definition-conormal-sheaf and preceding construction for immersions; Morphisms Tag 07RK, lemma-immersion-permanence (1)

proof.text: The canonical map $Y_U\to Y$ identifies $Y_U$ with the open $U\times_T Z_U$: because both factors map into $V$, the fibre product over $V$ equals the one over $T$. Its openness follows by applying [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] to the two open inclusions. The inverse image under $s$ of this open is exactly $Z_U$. Put $O_U=W\cap Y_U$. The two closed immersions $Z_U\hookrightarrow Y_U$ and $Z\hookrightarrow W$ restrict on $O_U$ to the same closed immersion $Z_U\hookrightarrow O_U$. An open immersion is flat: by [def-weil-open-immersion] its local-ring maps are isomorphisms, so the module in [def-weil-flat-morphism] is the rank-one free module over that same ring. Apply [lem-pur-conormal-algebra-flat-base-change] to $O_U\to Y_U$ and $O_U\to W$. The centre maps are respectively $1_{Z_U}$ and $Z_U\to Z$. This gives a graded algebra isomorphism $\alpha_U:G|_{Z_U}\xrightarrow{\sim}G(s_U)$. Its affine formula sends a homogeneous ideal class to its restriction, exactly the formula $[a]\otimes r\mapsto[g^\sharp(a)r]$ in that cited statement.

source.place: Tags 0634 and 0635, lemma-conormal-algebra-functorial and lemma-conormal-algebra-functorial-flat; Schemes Tag 01JY, open base change

proof.text: For a refinement $(U',V')$ of $(U,V)$, the restrictions in the preceding step carry $[a]$ to $[a|]$ in every degree. Hence the comparison obtained through $\alpha_U$ and $\alpha_{U'}$ is the direct restriction comparison. On any overlap $Z_U\cap Z_{U'}$ define the transition as $\alpha_{U'}\alpha_U^{-1}$, with both maps restricted to that overlap. This has identity when the indices coincide, inverse upon reversing them, and on triple overlaps its two composites agree by cancellation of $\alpha_{U'}^{-1}\alpha_{U'}$. Every comparison preserves products and units, since restriction sends $ab$ to $a|\,b|$ and $1$ to $1$. On affine refinements these are precisely the homogeneous-class maps required in the statement. We use affine covers of the overlaps, never assume an intersection is affine.

source.place: Tags 0633–0635, affine restriction formulas for the conormal algebra

proof.text: The $Z_U$ cover $Z$, and the isomorphisms $\alpha_U$ identify the displayed local algebras, their products and their units with restrictions of the already constructed $G$. Thus $G$ is their gluing. This gluing is independent of the affine cover: use the union of two covers and the same transition maps of the preceding step. It is also independent of the choice of $W$: for a second closed neighbourhood $W'$ compare both with $W\cap W'$ by the same open flat-base-change maps of [lem-pur-conormal-algebra-flat-base-change]. Each comparison is the identity on restricted ideal representatives; consequently the pairwise comparisons have identity and cocycle laws, by the same cancellation calculation as above. Set $\mathcal G(f,i)=G$. Its quasi-coherence and its degree-zero identification are those already supplied by [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra].

source.place: Tags 0630, 0633 and 0635, construction, affine compatibility and flat restriction of the conormal algebra

proof.text: Apply [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists] to the quasi-coherent graded algebra $G$: this gives $P(f,i)=\operatorname{Proj}_Z G$ with the asserted restrictions over every affine open of $Z$, hence in particular over each affine $Z_U$. Indeed $Z_U$ is affine by Step 1. The restriction maps are those induced by the same graded restrictions, and their compatibility and independence of affine choices are included in the cited existence statement. A degree-preserving algebra isomorphism induces the corresponding Proj isomorphism by [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] (2). Thus all the algebra identifications above also identify the corresponding relative Proj schemes over the centres.

source.place: Tag 01NQ, lemma-glue-relative-proj; functoriality of Proj under graded isomorphisms, Tags 01MY and 01MZ

proof.text: An isomorphism of diagrams $Z\hookrightarrow X\to T$ identifies their fibre products and graphs by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Transport a closed neighbourhood $W$ across this isomorphism. The resulting ambient isomorphism and its centre form a cartesian square, and it is flat because its local-ring maps are isomorphisms. The graded comparison of [lem-pur-conormal-algebra-flat-base-change] is therefore an isomorphism; on representatives it is $[a]\mapsto[h^\sharp(a)]$. Changing neighbourhoods agrees with Step 5. Identity and composition follow on these representatives from $(h\circ k)^\sharp=k^\sharp h^\sharp$, in every degree, including degree zero. The induced Proj maps of [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] (2) have the same laws: on a standard homogeneous chart their ring maps send $b/a^m$ to $h^\sharp(b)/h^\sharp(a)^m$, and successive substitutions compose. These charts cover Proj, so the identities hold globally. This establishes the specified canonical functoriality, including compatibility with the structural projections.

source.place: Tags 0634–0635, specified functorial conormal maps; Constructions Tags 01MY–01MZ, homogeneous localization maps

proof.text: Now assume $f$ is locally of finite type and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ is the specified first-Fitting singular inclusion. Use exactly the coborder closed neighbourhood and ideal $J$ of [def-sfb-nodal-branch-scheme]. Step 5 identifies $G$ with this closed graph's conormal algebra. The cited definition specifies $B_f=\operatorname{Bl}_J(W)\times_W Z$ and its presentation as the relative Proj of $\bigoplus J^n/J^{n+1}$. Here is the quotient calculation underlying that presentation, to make the identification explicit: on $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset W$, with ideal $I$, the blowup model is $\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal R_A(I))$ by [def-nagata-affine-blowup] and [def-nagata-rees-algebra]. Arbitrary relative-Proj base change [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary], applied to $A\to A/I$, gives the Proj of $\mathcal R_A(I)\otimes_A A/I$. In degree $n$ the canonical quotient is $I^n\otimes_A A/I=I^n/I I^n=I^n/I^{n+1}$, sending $a\otimes\bar r$ to $ar\bmod I^{n+1}$. This preserves the degree-zero unit and multiplication, and commutes with all affine restrictions because both operations just restrict $a$ and $r$. Hence it is the very conormal presentation specified in [def-sfb-nodal-branch-scheme], not an abstract isomorphism of fibres. By Step 6 its Proj is canonically $P(f,i)$ over $Z$, and the degree-zero map shows its projection is $p_f$. None of these arguments used nodality, flatness of $f$, or quasi-compactness.
